title: Mila and the Pointy Teeth
markdown:
In a cozy room, a lamp glowed like a sleepy moon. Blocks waited in a quiet pile, as if they knew Mila loved to build. Her friends were Pip the duck and Gran Ada, whose hugs were warm and comforting.

One gentle evening, they met a new friend: a long green puppet crocodile with many pointy teeth. “What does he like to eat?” asked Gran Ada softly.

Mila looked at the puppet’s mouth. “So many pointy teeth!” she whispered.

Pip quacked, “What are they for?”

Gran Ada smiled. “Our flat teeth mash soft foods, like bananas. But the crocodile’s teeth are sharp and pointy. What do you think they are for?”

They saw soft mashed strawberries. Pip nudged one. “Would he like these?”

Mila shook her head. “His teeth look like they’re for something special. Maybe for holding onto crunchy seeds or soft leaves?”

Pip chirped, “Like these little cracker crumbs?” He showed them tiny pieces.

Gran Ada nodded. “Every animal’s teeth help them eat the foods that keep them healthy. The crocodile’s teeth are perfect for his food, just like ours are for ours.”

Mila looked at plump juicy berries. “I think,” she whispered, “his pointy teeth are just perfect for gently holding these lovely soft berries, and then munching them up!”

Gran Ada held a berry to the puppet’s mouth. A tiny pretend nibble, and the berry was gone. The pointy teeth held it so nicely, as if they had been waiting for that job all day.

“See?” Gran Ada said gently. “The crocodile’s teeth help him enjoy his favourite foods, just like our teeth help us enjoy our warm porridge and sweet apples. It all makes sense.”

Pip quacked. “His teeth are for eating! And he likes berries!”

Mila saw how content the happy crocodile looked. She understood that even teeth had a clever purpose. The world, she realised, was full of wonderful ways for everything to be just right.

The lamp glowed softly. Mila felt her eyelids grow heavy, her mind full of the quiet wonders of teeth and food. She wondered what other mouths were hiding their own clever tools—another shape, another favourite, another way to be just right.
characters: Mila (curious builder), Pip (soft duck), Ada (warm-hug gran)
